detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=kube`.
• Install and configure Splunk Connect for Kubernetes / cloud provider K8s audit inputs with the modular input for `kube:objects:replicasets`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.9.1.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure required cloud inputs per provider guide; index=kube sourcetype=kube:objects:replicasets.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=kube sourcetype="kube:objects:replicasets" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=kube sourcetype="kube:objects:replicasets" verb=delete OR verb=DELETE
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.9.12_kubernetes_replicasets_d_12"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `kube:objects:replicasets` in `index=kube` to detect kubernetes replicasets delete events. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_9_12_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Dashboard panel, alert, and weekly compliance report..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk Connect for Kubernetes / cloud provider K8s audit inputs and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
